segments.source: Use the rules exactly as written. AND requires all listed conditions; OR requires at least one. A one-way implication cannot automatically be reversed. For the cross-domain check, independent reports = total reports − duplicate copies.
Which consequences can be deduced by applying the rules exactly? Do not assume the converse of any rule. Cross-domain check: how many non-duplicate reports remain?

1. Rain and high river satisfy both conditions of the first rule. 2. Infer flooding. 3. Flooding implies road closure. 4. The working siren independently implies a warning. Cross-domain check: 7−4=3 independent reports remain.
Flooding, road closure, and a warning can be deduced. Cross-domain answer: 3 independent reports.
Causal reasoning becomes clearer when every link is stated and the direction of implication is respected.
Forward-chaining rule system over Boolean facts; apply implications until no new facts appear.
Many explanations can be represented as condition-and-consequence rules. The logical form matters: necessary, sufficient, AND, and OR are not interchangeable.

Facts: Rain occurred; The river was not high; The warning siren worked; The gate was closed. Rules: If rain occurs AND the river is already high, flooding occurs. If flooding occurs, the riverside road closes. If the siren works, residents receive a warning. Cross-domain check: on a field sketch, 1 cm represents 4 km and two checkpoints are 7 cm apart.

Use the rules exactly as written. AND requires all listed conditions; OR requires at least one. A one-way implication cannot automatically be reversed. For the cross-domain check, real distance = sketch distance × kilometres per centimetre.
Which consequences can be deduced by applying the rules exactly? Do not assume the converse of any rule. Cross-domain check: what real distance separates the checkpoints?

1. Rain is true but the high-river condition is false. 2. The AND rule for flooding therefore does not fire. 3. Without flooding, road closure is not inferred. 4. The siren rule still gives a warning. Cross-domain check: 7×4=28 km.
A warning can be deduced, but flooding and road closure cannot be deduced. Cross-domain answer: 28 km.

Facts: Rain occurred; The river was already high; The warning siren worked; The gate was closed; Flooding occurred. Rules: If rain occurs AND the river is already high, flooding occurs. If flooding occurs, the riverside road closes. If the siren works, residents receive a warning. Cross-domain check: a survey team starts work at 12:00 and works for 2 hour(s) without a break.

Use the rules exactly as written. AND requires all listed conditions; OR requires at least one. A one-way implication cannot automatically be reversed. For the cross-domain check, finishing time = starting time + duration.
Which consequences can be deduced by applying the rules exactly? Do not assume the converse of any rule. Cross-domain check: at what time does the team finish?

1. Flooding is stated directly, so apply the flooding→road-closure rule. 2. Apply siren→warning. 3. Do not use flooding to infer rain or a high river; that would reverse a rule. Cross-domain check: 12+2=14, so the team finishes at 14:00.
Road closure and a warning can be deduced; flooding is already given as a fact. Cross-domain answer: 14:00.
